content: 1. Indinavir increases the levels of clomipramine by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, which is responsible for its metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 2. Indinavir increases the levels of clonazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to the potential for increased toxicity. Consider alternative therapies or lowering the benzodiazepine dose. 3. Indinavir decreases the levels and efficacy of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4, which reduces clopidogrel bioactivation. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Indinavir increases the levels of clorazepate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised due to the potential for increased toxicity. Consider alternative therapies or reducing the benzodiazepine dose. 5. Clotrimazole decreases the levels and efficacy of indinavir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Indinavir increases the levels of clozapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Conivaptan increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Indinavir increases the levels of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Indinavir increases the levels of vaginal conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Indinavir increases the levels of cortisone by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Indinavir increases the levels of crizotinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Crizotinib increases the levels of indinavir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Crofelemer increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer is unlikely to inhibit systemic CYP3A4 due to minimal absorption but may inhibit it in the gut. 14. Indinavir increases the levels of cyclophosphamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Indinavir increases the levels of cyclosporine by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Dabrafenib decreases the levels and efficacy of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Danicopan increases the levels of indinavir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Danicopan increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates, and dose reduction of these substrates should be considered to avoid serious adverse reactions. 18. Darifenacin increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Indinavir increases the levels of darolutamide by affecting other mechanisms, including CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Darolutamide is a substrate of both CYP3A4 and P-gp, and dose adjustments may be necessary to avoid adverse reactions. 20. Darunavir increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases the levels of darunavir by the same mechanism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Dasatinib increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases the levels of dasatinib by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Deferasirox decreases the levels and efficacy of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Indinavir increases the levels of deflazacort by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Indinavir increases the levels of desvenlafaxine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 25. Indinavir increases the levels of dexamethasone by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. DHEA (herbal) increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Indinavir increases the levels of diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to the potential for increased toxicity. Consider alternative therapies or lowering the benzodiazepine dose. 28. Indinavir increases the levels of buccal diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 29. Indinavir increases the levels of intranasal diazepam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease diazepam elimination, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 30. Indinavir increases the effects of diazoxide, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Didanosine decreases the levels and efficacy of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer indinavir one hour prior to didanosine chewable tablets or powder. No significant interactions are reported with didanosine capsules. 32. Indinavir increases the levels of dienogest/estradiol valerate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. HIV protease inhibitors may cause significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin, leading to potential adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 33. Indinavir increases the levels of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Diltiazem increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Indinavir increases the levels of dofetilide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to the potential for increased toxicity, including QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 36. Indinavir increases the levels of doravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. 37. Indinavir increases the levels of doxepin cream by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Indinavir increases the levels of doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Indinavir increases the levels of liposomal doxorubicin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Indinavir increases the levels of dronabinol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. 41. Dronedarone increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Indinavir increases the levels of duvelisib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to the increased risk of duvelisib toxicities. 43. Duvelisib increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended due to the increased risk of toxicities of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 44. Indinavir and efavirenz both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Elagolix increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Indinavir increases the levels of elagolix by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 46. Indinavir increases the levels of eletriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Indinavir increases the levels of elvitegravir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase its levels. 48. Indinavir and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Encorafenib affects indinavir by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents. 50. Indinavir increases the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is metabolized by CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, leading to higher toxicity. 51. Indinavir and enfuvirtide both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Indinavir increases the levels of erlotinib by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Erythromycin base increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Indinavir increases the levels of escitalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity and the risk of serotonin syndrome. 58. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases the levels and efficacy of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Indinavir increases the levels of estradiol by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Indinavir increases the levels of vaginal estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and their toxicities. 61. Indinavir increases the levels of synthetic conjugated estrogens by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Indinavir increases the levels of esterified estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Indinavir increases the levels of estropipate by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 64. Indinavir increases the levels of eszopiclone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day. 65. Indinavir increases the levels of ethosuximide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Indinavir increases the levels of etonogestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Indinavir increases the levels of etoposide by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Indinavir increases the levels of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Indinavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution by causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Indinavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable suspension by causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Fedratinib increases the levels of indinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
